item.title: Two-Stage Stochastic Portfolio Optimization via the L-Shaped Method
item.description: Two-stage stochastic program (SAA over 500 bootstrap scenarios from real ETF data) with CVaR risk linearized per Rockafellar–Uryasev; solved via the L-shaped (Benders) method and progressive hedging.

item.title: Large-Scale Portfolio Optimization: Cardinality-Constrained MIQP & Lagrangian Relaxation
item.description: Extends Markowitz mean-variance optimization to the NP-hard cardinality-constrained setting (hold ≤ K assets): exact MIQP via Gurobi, and Lagrangian relaxation with Polyak subgradient updates for large universes — validated on S&P 500 constituent data.

item.title: About
item.description:
I am Meiqi Zhang, a Financial Mathematics & Statistics graduate from the University of Sydney (GPA 4.0, Dalyell Scholar), and an incoming M.Sc. Computer Science student at the University of Hong Kong (Delta X Tech Immersion Fellowship).

My work sits at the intersection of mathematical optimization, stochastic programming, and quantitative finance — from cardinality-constrained portfolio MIQP solved via Lagrangian relaxation, to two-stage stochastic programs solved with the L-shaped method, to LLM-guided reinforcement learning for portfolio management. I am actively seeking graduate study and research opportunities in operations research and quantitative modeling.

item.title: Research
item.description:
My research spans optimization, quantitative finance, and human–AI interaction, with a consistent interest in turning rigorous models into decisions under uncertainty. Several directions also appear as runnable code on the Projects page.

Large-Scale Portfolio Optimization: Cardinality-Constrained MIQP & Lagrangian Relaxation Link to heading

Feb – Apr 2026

  • Extends Markowitz mean-variance optimization to the NP-hard cardinality-constrained setting (hold ≤ K assets): exact MIQP via Gurobi, and Lagrangian relaxation with Polyak subgradient updates for large universes — validated on S&P 500 constituent data.
  • Lagrangian decomposition: convex QP x-subproblem (CVXPY/OSQP) + closed-form greedy z-subproblem; <2% optimality gap at a fraction of MIQP solve time.
  • Scalability study N = 50 → 500, rolling out-of-sample backtest, Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage, and a robust-optimization extension with ellipsoidal uncertainty sets.
